correctness.rationale: The exact one-step equations imply a uniform deterministic two-step bound on |X|. For h>mu/(1-d) they reduce, after finite time, to iid fair signs. Each two-step affine composition has Euclidean Lipschitz factor d<1, giving uniqueness and coupling convergence. The independent even/odd stationary scalar affine expansions yield the product invariant law. The scalar interval images have a positive gap exactly for d<1/2, meet at d=1/2, and overlap to fill the invariant interval for d>1/2. Strong separation gives the doubled Hausdorff dimension below threshold; the critical half-interval partition yields exact uniform planar density. A finite maximal-atom argument proves the scalar stationary law is nonatomic. At even lags the conditional joint law lies on a finite union of graphs; at odd lags disjoint sign parity gives independence. Nonatomicity gives TV 1 and infinite mutual information at even lags, while exact conditional first and second moments give all-zero linear covariance and positive d^(2k) quadratic memory. Exact-rational check.py ran with VERIFY_OK. Numerical outputs are not used for infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The exact same published stochastic switching-surface model exhibits a natural dimension/support phase transition with an explicit full-dimensional invariant density at the critical point; the limiting stationary geometry alone cannot reveal its finite-lag temporal dependence. Despite a smooth planar stationary density at d=1/2 and zero coordinate autocovariance at all nonzero lags, every even-lag two-time law remains mutually singular with independence whereas odd lags are exactly independent. The positive quadratic-memory coefficient quantifies the hidden causal memory. The result gives a complete parameter and lag classification for a canonical symmetric, high-noise subfamily and a useful warning against using linear correlations to infer loss of dependence; the general scalar IFS dimension lemma alone would be insufficient as the entire contribution.
